newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine approves gas trading scheme, 1997 imports.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine approves gas trading scheme, 1997 imports.

text.p: Ukraine's State Oil and Gas Committee has approved a list of gas importers and forecast total 1997 domestic gas demand at 81.2 billion cubic metres (bcm), a senior energy official said on Friday.
The official, who asked not to be named, said Ukraine would buy 53 bcm of the total from Russia.
Kiev is also to import 10-12 bcm from the Central Asia states of Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan in a bid to diversify suppliers.
Ukraine's domestic gas output is forecast to be flat at 17 bcm this year.
The official also said that a gas trading system inside the country of 52 million was approved on Thursday.

The country's biggest gas trader, the United Energy Systems of Ukraine (UESU), based in the eastern industrial city of Dnipropetrovsk, was awarded the largest share of gas for trading on Ukraine's market -- 15.5 bcm.
The UESU will supply gas to the two most economically powerful regions -- Dnipropetrovsk and Donetsk, home to many heavy industrial enterprises.

In 1995 the government set up a scheme obliging both private and state companies to supply gas to Ukraine from Russian gas monopoly Gazprom GAZP.RTS and Central Asian sources and to collect debts for unpaid gas.

The government praised the scheme, which, it said, allowed Ukraine to pay off almost all of its debts to Gazprom. Kiev still owes $1.5 billion for 1993-94 supplies and will pay the sum over eight years.

The Itera-Ukraine company, which mostly imports Turkmen gas, won the right to sell between six billion and eight billion cubic metres on Ukraine's market. Intergaz company was awarded 5.8 billion cubic metres of Russian gas.
The recently-created Ukrainian Gas Consortium (UGC) got 8.0 bcm.
The Newly-formed Gazpex company will import at least 4.5 billion cubic metres of gas from Uzbekistan. Last month Uzbekistan agreed to supply Ukraine with up to 10 bcm of gas annually.
Further amounts will be sold by several minor traders.
Ukraine's President Leonid Kuchma said in 1996 that there should be no monopoly on the domestic gas market and blamed government leadership for protecting particular traders.
